data.topic: developer lifecycle best practices with AI — software factory patterns, AI-augmented SDLC, orchestration and decomposition, codebase intelligence, quality verification, human-AI trust

claims.claim: Industry converging on six-component factory: Orchestrator, Planner/Reasoning Engine, Sandbox Executor, Agent-Computer Interface, Memory (vector+RAG), Verification Pipeline. StrongDM, GitHub Copilot Workspace, Factory.ai independently arrived at nearly identical decompositions.

StrongDM Dark Factory: Level 5 autonomous — no human code writing or review. Components: Attractor (coding agent), holdout BDD scenarios (invisible to agent), Digital Twin Universe (third-party service clones), CXDB (immutable DAG), Evaluator (separate validation agent). Train/test isolation prevents test gaming.
Microsoft AI-led SDLC: Spec Kit (accepts prompt + organizational constitution, outputs structured tasks) → GitHub Copilot Coding Agent → Code Quality Review → GitHub Actions → SRE Agent.

Three competing architectures: (1) Multi-agent symphony (Google Jules, Amazon Kira, Factory.ai), (2) Single-threaded master loop (Claude Code), (3) Static pipeline/Agentless ($0.34/issue vs $10+). Winning pattern depends on task complexity.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) emerging as universal standard for agent tool/context discovery. GitHub/Microsoft deprecated older extension models Nov 2025 in favor of MCP.
Shared state backbone — not the LLM itself — is the critical architectural differentiator: OpenHands pub/sub Event Stream, Factory.ai CI/CD-triggered Droids, StrongDM CXDB.
JM Family deployed BAQA Genie: 5 specialized agents (requirements, story writing, coding, documentation, QA). Cut requirements+test design from weeks to days, saved 60% QA time.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: The factory pattern has identifiable, converging components across independent implementations. The critical architectural invariant is train/test isolation: the code generation subsystem must be completely isolated from the verification subsystem to prevent test gaming.

claims.claim: AgentConductor (Feb 2025): dynamic DAG topology outperforms fixed-topology baselines by up to 14.6% pass@1 on APPS (58.8% vs 44.9%) while reducing token usage 68%. Key: density-aware scaling to task difficulty.
Hierarchical validation gates improve iteration success rates from 22.6% to 41.1%. Per-step validation matters more than graph topology itself.

BMAD v6.1.0: 19+ specialized agents, 50+ workflows, spec-first sequential handoffs. 55% faster complex task completion, 90% token reduction via document sharding. Takes 5.5hrs vs 15min vibe coding but produces stable auditable code.
Ralph: stateless iterative loops with Git as memory and backpressure gates (tests, linting, type-checking). Fresh AI instance each iteration prevents context drift.

Claude Code agent teams: dependency-ordered tasks with auto-unblock. But official docs warn that sequential tasks or highly interdependent work should use single-session subagents — DAG not universally superior to sequential.
SWE-bench Verified (March 2026): Claude Sonnet 5 at 82.1%, Opus 4.5 at 80.9%. Planning-based agents score 10-20% higher on long-horizon multi-module tasks vs reactive agents.
Minimalist agentless approaches sometimes outperform complex multi-agent on simpler benchmarks. Complexity is not always beneficial.
CodePlan (Microsoft Research) builds dependency graphs via AST and class hierarchy for Change May-Impact Analysis, orders edits using topological sorting.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: The three orchestration archetypes (structured DAG, sequential handoff, stateless loop) each dominate different problem shapes. But per-step validation gates — not the topology — are the critical differentiator, nearly doubling iteration success rates.

claims.claim: ReVeal (MSRA, June 2025): iterative generation-verification loop improves pass@1 from 36.9% to 42.4% over 19 turns. 10.56% of incorrect solutions self-correct, only 0.18% degrade. Model trained on 3 turns surpasses larger models at 20+ inference turns.

Foundational self-repair architecture: Generator, Executor (sandbox), Critic/Reflector, Episodic Memory. Established by Self-Debug, Reflexion, LEVER (2023). The shift is from LLM-as-Judge to Environment-as-Judge.
Aider: Architect/Editor pattern, auto-runs linters+tests after every edit, retries up to 6 times. 88% on Polyglot benchmark.
Fault-tolerant sandbox: 100% interception rate for high-risk commands, 100% rollback success, only 14.5% latency overhead (~1.8s/transaction) using copy-on-write filesystem snapshots.
Diminishing returns beyond 3-5 repair iterations (NeurIPS 2024). Balancing initial generation quality with limited repair yields superior results vs more iterations.

SWE-bench resolve rates: ~18% single-agent 2024 → 53-79% multi-agent 2025-2026 with sandboxed CI. But SWE-CI shows zero-regression rates below 0.25 on long-horizon CI maintenance — isolated tasks pass, cumulative correctness degrades.
25% of devs estimate 1-in-5 AI suggestions contain errors (Qodo, n=609). Teams using AI code review: 81% report quality improvement vs 55% without.
Spec-Driven Development (SDD): agents generate specs + acceptance tests BEFORE implementation. PR gate only opens if agent provides logs proving tests passed in sandbox.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: 80% first-run CI pass rate requires high-quality initial generation plus bounded self-repair (3-5 iterations), not unbounded loops. The self-healing loop itself is the primary quality driver — iteration count matters more than model size. But cumulative correctness across commits degrades even when single-task pass rates are high.

claims.claim: Industry standard is Three-Index Fusion: BM25 keyword + vector embeddings + structural graph (AST/SCIP). Removing graph component degrades cross-file F1 by 4-6%.
GraphCoder: Code Context Graph with control flow + data dependence + control dependence edges. +6.06% Exact Match, +6.23% Identifier EM over RepoCoder on RepoEval. Language-agnostic via tree-sitter.
Sourcegraph Cody deprecated embeddings for Enterprise due to privacy/scaling. Current: BM25 via Zoekt + SCIP/LSIF semantic graph. Deep Cody adds multi-hop agentic retrieval.
Voyage-Code-3 outperforms OpenAI text-embedding-3-large by 13.8% across 32 code retrieval datasets. Supports 32K context, Matryoshka embeddings, binary quantization for 384x storage reduction.
Aider RepoMap: tree-sitter symbols → file dependency graph → PageRank ranking → compressed skeleton maps within token budgets (~1024 tokens).

Convention enforcement via hierarchical instruction: Cursor .cursorrules (MDC+glob), GitHub copilot-instructions.md (personal>repo>org priority). Automatic inference from code is unsolved in production.
RepoCoder: generate-then-retrieve iterative loop improves repository-level style alignment by 10%+. Convention compliance treated as retrieval problem, not rule-matching.
Structural collapsing: keep class structure + method signatures visible, replace irrelevant bodies with placeholders. Preserves architectural context while saving thousands of tokens.
Tree-sitter AST-aware chunking: up to 82% improvement in retrieval precision over fixed-size chunking (cAST research).

synthesized_findings.key_insight: No single retrieval method suffices — hybrid three-index fusion is the standard. But the defining 2024-2025 shift is from single-pass retrieval to agentic multi-hop context curation (Deep Cody, Greptile v3). Convention extraction from code remains unsolved in production — current tools use explicit developer-authored rules, not learned inference.

claims.claim: Trust-adoption paradox: 84% usage, 29% trust (2025). Down 11pts from 2024. 96% don't fully trust AI code, but only 48% always verify before committing.

38% say reviewing AI code requires MORE effort than human code. Reviewers miss 40% more bugs in AI code due to 'veneer of correctness' (perfect syntax, logical errors). Complex AI PRs wait 4.6x longer in review queues.
Reviewing the conversation/plan matters as much as the diff. The human reviewer role shifts from line-by-line inspection to understanding intent and risk.
PR Contract pattern: intent, proof of functionality, risk tier, review focus areas. Qodo PR-Agent implements structured walkthrough with mandatory rationale per hunk.
Progressive autonomy: Shadow Mode → Review-First → Sandboxed Autonomy → Permission Escalation. Situational autonomy (dynamic adjustment by context) produces best team performance (CHI 2024).
Adaptive verbal cues outperform continuous transparency displays for trust calibration. Override rates shift from 17% to 63% with adaptive warnings.
Trust asymmetry: 3 positive recommendations to build trust, 1 bad one to lose it.
AI-generated code requires 2x more rework within 30-90 days despite 80-90% initial acceptance rate. GitClear: 39.9% decrease in refactoring, 8x increase in duplicated code attributed to AI.
Three design dimensions for trust: communicating AI performance, allowing preference configuration, offering mechanism indicators to support validation.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: The velocity gained during AI-assisted authoring is neutralized by downstream review bottlenecks: higher cognitive load, 4.6x longer review queues, 40% more missed bugs. Sustainable trust requires structured verification contracts (plan-first, rationale, impact matrices) and progressive autonomy — not just better code.

key_insights: Six-component canonical factory architecture converging independently across implementations
Train/test isolation is the critical architectural invariant
Shared state backbone matters more than LLM capability
DAG, sequential, and stateless loops each dominate different problem shapes
Per-step validation gates nearly double iteration success
Minimalist approaches sometimes beat complex multi-agent
Self-healing loops are the primary quality driver
Cumulative correctness degrades even when single-task pass rates are high
Agentic multi-hop retrieval is the 2024-2025 shift
Convention extraction from code is unsolved in production
Structured verification contracts and progressive autonomy are emerging solutions

gemini_claim.claim: DAG-based planning outperforms by 10-20% on long-horizon multi-module tasks

claude_claim.claim: Claude Code docs explicitly warn sequential tasks should use single-session subagents, not teams. DAG not universally superior.

conflicts.credibility_assessment: Both are valid — they apply to different task shapes. DAG wins for parallel-decomposable work, sequential wins for highly interdependent changes. The task's dependency structure determines the right topology.

conflicts.topic: Value of iteration count in self-repair

gemini_claim.claim: ReVeal model continues improving over 20+ turns at inference, surpassing larger models

claude_claim.claim: NeurIPS 2024 repair research shows diminishing or negative returns beyond moderate retry budgets (3-5 iterations)

conflicts.credibility_assessment: Both peer-reviewed. ReVeal uses a specifically RL-trained verification loop; the NeurIPS paper tests general-purpose LLMs. The takeaway: trained self-repair loops sustain value at high iterations, general-purpose LLM retry does not.

gaps: No head-to-head benchmark comparing DAG vs sequential vs unconstrained on identical codebases
Convention inference from code (without explicit rules) is unsolved in production
No cost-benefit analysis of self-healing loop iterations vs quality gains
Cross-language polyglot microservice mapping largely unexplored
No longitudinal data on AI-driven code duplication's impact on maintainability
Capturing architectural rationale from non-code sources (PRs, docs, meetings) — all current systems only extract from code
